title: Bring the Tumbler's small controls up to the 24 px target floor
body:
## Summary
The Tumbler's controls are 20-22 px, under the 24 px target floor tokens.css itself names.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/design/tokens.css:117 sets --ctl-sm: 24px as "the 24px target floor"; the Tumbler block (apps/desktop/client/src/design/tokens.css:190) lowers it to 22px, so every sm button on the card, stack and welcome (Review and decide, Withdraw, the info buttons, Always on top, Do not disturb, Later, Got it) is 22 px. apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/tumbler.css:114 makes the card pager arrows 22 px wide; tumbler.css:319-321 makes each first-run step link 20 px tall in a 20 px grid with no spacing. WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 (target size minimum) asks 24 x 24 or equivalent spacing. The forms are fixed grids inside Rust's window sizes (Form::size), so the fix must fit: card row 4 grows 28 -> 30 px (card content ends at 139 of 152); the first-run welcome's steps 80 -> 96 px is the tight one (228 px window).

## Flow
- census: count interactive elements in tumbler.css / the Tumbler token block under 24 px (today: sm buttons 22, pager arrows 22, step links 20)
- raise --ctl-sm to 24px in the Tumbler block, .nav .ui-btn.arr to 24px, .fr-step / .fr-steps rows to 24px
- re-fit the card (grid-template-rows row 4) and the first-run welcome (rows or the promise clamp) so every row still ends inside 440x152 / 440x228, puck top and bottom
- verify in the browser preview at each form

## Expected impact
A pointer or touch user hits the Tumbler's buttons reliably; the gold Review, Withdraw and the step links stop being the smallest targets in the product. Could break: the fixed-grid row arithmetic beside the puck corner.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every Tumbler target at least 24 px
Before: 3 control classes under 24 px (sm buttons 22, pager 22, step links 20)
After: predicted 0, if the first-run welcome grid can absorb 16 px
Method: simulation - row sums walked for the card (139/152 after) and the welcome (about 6 px over unless the promise row shrinks); the layout instrument is a browser probe this round may not run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/design/tokens.css:117  --ctl-sm: 24px;     /* inline, toolbar-dense: the 24px target floor */
apps/desktop/client/src/design/tokens.css:190  --row: 28px; --row-2: 44px; --ctl: 26px; --ctl-sm: 22px; --bar: 38px;   (Tumbler block)
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/tumbler.css:114  .nav .ui-btn.arr { width: 22px; ...
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/tumbler.css:319  .fr-steps { ... grid-auto-rows: 20px; }
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/tumbler.css:321  .fr-step { width: 100%; height: 20px; ...
instrument: vitest census over tumbler.css + the Tumbler token block: interactive selectors with height/width < 24px (seed: put .fr-step back to 20px -> red), plus the browser preview frame at each FORM_SIZE checking no row overflows its form (scrollHeight <= height) with the puck top and bottom

title: Docs still describe the removed card id link and the module hex colour
body:
## Summary
window-duality.md describes a Tumbler card id link the card no longer has, and shared/ui/README.md names a MODULE[m].color hex field that was removed.

## Description
docs/design/window-duality.md:128-130 says "Open in Table moved to the id link (D-0193 ↗)" and "the deadline is a 2px rule". The card has no id link (its CSS, .c-id, had zero consumers and was removed this round, 3a3f4ac) and draws the deadline as a ring around the amount whenever the question carries one (forms.tsx AmountRing; the 2 px rule only without one). apps/desktop/client/src/shared/ui/README.md:11 says MODULE[m].color (hex) is for the Dial / Tumbler art; ModuleMeta has no color field (shared/modules.tsx), the art uses cssVar tokens. AGENTS.md tells agents to read window-duality.md before changing behaviour.

## Flow
- edit window-duality.md (and its HTML twin if it carries the paragraph): Open in The Table and Let it lapse live in the details popover; the deadline is a ring around the amount, the 2 px rule only without an amount
- edit shared/ui/README.md: module colour is cssVar only
- grep both claims -> 0

## Expected impact
Agents and people reading the design docs stop building against a card element that does not exist. Doc-only; nothing at runtime can break.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the docs agree with the shipped card and module metadata
Before: 2 stale claims (window-duality.md:128-130, shared/ui/README.md:11)
After: 0 by the same grep
Method: probe - both claims checked against the code this round; the files are outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
docs/design/window-duality.md:129  Table" moved to the id link (`D-0193 ↗`) and the ⓘ details popover ...
docs/design/window-duality.md:130  deadline caption; the deadline is a 2px rule with 15 min / 2 h ticks.
apps/desktop/client/src/shared/ui/README.md:11  ... `MODULE[m].color` (hex) is only for the fixed-palette Dial / Tumbler art.
apps/desktop/client/src/shared/modules.tsx: ModuleMeta = { key, name, long, cssVar }

title: Load the Tumbler preview chunks through lazyPart instead of raw React.lazy
body:
## Summary
App.tsx loads the browser-preview stages with raw React.lazy and fallback={null}.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/App.tsx:8 and :10 use raw lazy() with fallback={null} where lib/lazy.ts offers lazyPart. Both chunks load only when backend().kind === 'mock' (a plain browser preview); the shipped window renders <Tumbler/> directly and never imports them.

## Flow
- swap the two lazy() calls for lazyPart with a shaped fallback

## Expected impact
None in the desktop window.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer blank frames on a cold Tumbler visit
Before: 0 raw-lazy sites on the shipped window's path (2 on the mock-only path)
After: 0 on the shipped path
Method: probe - read App.tsx: the branch is mock-only
Result: not-better
Gate: none
